title: Modern Color Spaces: OKLCH, Display P3 & Perceptual Uniformity
subtopicTitle: Modern Color Spaces: OKLCH, Display P3 & Perceptual Uniformity
problemStatement:
Why modern design systems are abandoning sRGB/hex in favor of OKLCH for perceptually uniform color palettes, accessible contrast calculations, and wide-gamut Display P3.

**Enterprise Importance**:
In sRGB/hex, 50% yellow looks bright white while 50% blue looks pitch dark. OKLCH fixes this with independent Lightness (L), Chroma (C), and Hue (H) ensuring predictable accessible contrast across all hues.
interviewTrap: Assuming hex #808080 or HSL lightness 50% has the same human perceived luminance across different colors. It does not.

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: OKLCH separates Lightness (0-100%), Chroma (saturation), and Hue (0-360 deg). Increasing hue from 0 to 360 keeps perceived lightness identical, enabling algorithmic palette generation with guaranteed WCAG contrast.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Design Token Layer: Primitives, semantic aliases, and component tokens established.
2. Component Architecture: Headless state and keyboard accessibility hooks implemented.
3. Styling & Cascade: Zero-runtime CSS variables and layer specificity managed.
4. Governance & Packaging: Tree-shaking, semantic versioning, and telemetry monitored.
